events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Grand Haven: 3 (good).** Go here first, by boat. Run spoons 55-110 ft down in 120-210 ft of water.
- **South Haven: 2 (average).** Your second choice. Run spoons near 110 ft of water.
- **Muskegon: 1 (below average).** Fishing was thin, with a few fish near the sand docks.
- **St. Joseph: 1 (below average).** Only a couple of boats were catching fish at the pier heads.
- **Lures:** green, yellow and orange spoons, plus green or white flies deeper in the water column.

## Why

- Grand Haven's latest boat report was good, with spoons and flies producing (Grand Haven, 2026-09-14). Note that the report is dated 2022-09-14, which is six days before today.
- South Haven's latest boat report was average, and its prior week was good (South Haven, 2022-09-14 and 2022-09-07).
- Muskegon and St. Joseph were both rated below average in the latest reports (Muskegon and St. Joseph, 2022-09-14).
- I'd expect Grand Haven to remain the best bet this week, since it has been the strongest port in the last two reports, but that is an inference from only two weeks of data.

## Evidence

**Recent reports** (newest is 2022-09-14, six days old)
- Grand Haven, 2022-09-14, boat: "The salmon action was decent 55 to 110 feet down in 120 to 210 feet of water." Quality 3. Spoons in green, yellow and orange, and green and white flies. The pier was slow (quality 0).
- South Haven, 2022-09-14, boat: "Boat anglers targeting salmon had decent fishing when they could get out." Quality 2. "The best water was around 110 feet of water," mostly on spoons.
- Muskegon, 2022-09-14, boat: "Boat anglers were finding salmon 55 to 100 feet down in 100 to 200 feet of water." Quality 1. Green and orange spoons, green flies.
- St. Joseph, 2022-09-14, boat: "There were a couple of boats fishing the pier heads and caught a couple of coho and Chinook." Quality 1.
- Earlier, 2022-09-07: South Haven was good (quality 3, fish at 110-120 ft and "the best water was around 40 feet"). Grand Haven and Muskegon were average (quality 2). St. Joseph was below average (quality 1).

**Past seasons**
- A search of earlier seasons for weeks with similar water temperature (about 71 F) returned only the same 2022 reports listed above. I have no independent history to add.

**Conditions now**
- Live conditions were unavailable. The tool returned only a backtest summary for the week before 2022-09-20: buoy surface water of about 70-71 F at all four ports, with little change over the week.
- No wind forecast or modeled cold-layer depth was available.

## Caveats

- The newest reports are six days old. Fall conditions can change quickly, so check the next DNR bulletin and the local wind forecast before going.
- I could not get a wind forecast. Check it before you launch. If it is strong, the piers and river mouths are the fallback.
- Surface temperature is from the buoy and is measured, but it is not the depth where salmon are holding. The reports suggest the fish are 55-110 ft down.
- The reports don't mention any launch or pier closures.

## Sources

- Grand Haven, Muskegon, South Haven, St. Joseph bulletin of 2022-09-14: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/32cff90
- Grand Haven, Muskegon, South Haven, St. Joseph bulletin of 2022-09-07: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/32bbcf0
- Bulletin of 2022-08-24 (background only): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3298204
